quotes.text: Learn how to set up your integration with Alma.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Alma is a [single-use](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods.md#usage) payment method where customers choose to pay between 2, 3, or 4 installments.
Provide a `return_url` when confirming a PaymentIntent with Alma.
The default local currency for Alma is `eur` and customers also see their purchase amount in `eur`.
An authentication session expires after 1 hour. You can refresh the QR code up to 20 times

findings: The November 7 capture is an index naming five parameterized variants: Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS and Android (new raw lines 9-18). It states no payment behavior, prerequisites, expiry, currency, capture or SDK details. The diff replaces the May full variant body with these links (diff lines 3-20, 1438-1443); this is a capture/navigation change, not evidence of functional removal or a new provider rule.

The May 6 old capture actually has five branches, including Android, at old raw lines 8-18, 108-112, 714-718, 946-952 and 1220-1226. The current source says four paths and leaves Android out at source line 13. The new index also lists Android (new raw lines 16-18), so the correction should restore this central route without claiming Android functionality was added in November.

The old guide describes Alma as single-use, 2/3/4 installments, redirect authorization and immediate outcome notification (old raw lines 18-18, 718-718, 1224-1226). Checkout hosted creates a Session with success_url; embedded Checkout uses return_url (old raw lines 33-38, 40-90). Elements and Direct API create server-side PaymentIntents, pass client secrets and confirm on the client; the manual redirect option confirms on the server then handles requires_action/next_action.redirect_to_url (old raw lines 127-173, 392-394, 733-749, 822-910). A redirect or client callback alone does not establish payment success; the old guide says inspect PaymentIntent status and listen for payment_intent.succeeded (old raw lines 488-497, 512-541, 669-673, 912-916).

The source's unqualified '`return_url` required for Alma' (source line 19) overreaches. The old error table requires return_url when confirming a PaymentIntent with Alma (old raw lines 703-712); hosted Checkout instead shows success_url, while embedded Checkout uses return_url (old raw lines 40-90). Narrow the subject to PaymentIntent confirmation and the applicable UI path. The same unqualified claim occurs in wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md lines 91 and 259 and wiki/stripe-index.md line 329. Propose reciprocal qualification in all three routes, as a May 6 historical claim; the November index supplies no current return_url rule (new raw lines 9-18).

The source's two authentication modes and 1-hour QR refresh claim (source lines 21-23) come from the old Elements branch (old raw lines 605-619), with separate mobile redirect and desktop QR conditions. Its 1-hour requires_action expiry and PaymentMethod detachment are documented at old raw lines 693-701; the brief source line 17 should not imply expiry of all PaymentIntents or compare other BNPL methods as if established by this raw. The 7-day manual-capture window is also conditional on capture_method:manual and requires_capture after authorization, with auto-cancel if uncaptured (old raw lines 621-651; source line 25).

The May mobile examples contain a material internal contradiction: iOS and Android Dashboard/dynamic PaymentIntent examples use currency usd (old raw lines 1051-1069, 1300-1317), while both branches' supported-currency tables list only eur and the Elements error table says Alma only supports eur (old raw lines 1194-1200, 1413-1419, 703-712). Do not infer USD Alma eligibility from example code. Android prose says PaymentHandler.confirmPayment while code uses PaymentLauncher.confirm (old raw lines 1362-1405); keep SDK wording version-qualified.

Old test flow distinguishes sandbox test approval/decline from live Alma redirect (old raw lines 687-691). Source line 27 only lists two of four old error codes; missing_required_parameter and payment_intent_payment_attempt_failed are at old raw lines 703-712, but this is detail navigable in the retained raw rather than an independent blocker.
substantive_changes: No substantive payment integration change is established by the November index (new raw lines 9-18). The needed source and reciprocal concept/index route update is dated provenance/navigation and correction of baseline route/scope errors: missing Android and unqualified return_url in wiki/sources/source-stripe-alma-accept-payment.md lines 13 and 19, wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md lines 91 and 259, and wiki/stripe-index.md line 329 (old raw lines 40-90, 703-712, 1220-1226).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain May 6, 2026 dated details for single-use 2/3/4-installment Alma, server-controlled amounts and eligible payment methods, Checkout same-currency line items, EUR documented support, client confirmation and redirects (old raw lines 18-38, 127-168, 733-749, 938-945). The November index is not refreshed behavioral authority (new raw lines 9-18).

Retain Elements-specific 1-hour mobile/desktop authentication, desktop QR up to 20 refreshes, expired requires_action to requires_payment_method with PaymentMethod detachment, manual capture requires_capture and 7-day cancellation, and payment_intent.succeeded event handling (old raw lines 605-673, 693-701). Do not generalize a browser return or modal closure to final funds/capture (old raw lines 488-497, 617-651).

Retain old iOS and Android branch as historical Mobile Payment Element guidance, with old iOS 13+ and Android SDK 23.7.0 sample versions; neither an old sample nor the November links proves current SDK support or merchant eligibility (old raw lines 946-971, 1220-1265; new raw lines 16-18).

Retain direct API optional manual redirect by requires_action/next_action.redirect_to_url and status verification, separate from server PaymentIntent creation or payment_intent.succeeded (old raw lines 733-749, 822-910, 912-916).
conflicts: Source line 13 says four paths and omits Android, conflicting with both old Android branch at old raw lines 1220-1226 and new index line 18. This is a pre-existing summary error, not a newly added variant.

wiki/sources/source-stripe-alma-accept-payment.md line 19, wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md lines 91 and 259, and wiki/stripe-index.md line 329 all say return_url is required for Alma without a flow subject. The May old requirement is specifically PaymentIntent confirmation (old raw lines 392-394, 703-712); hosted Checkout example uses success_url (old raw lines 40-63), while embedded Checkout has return_url (old raw lines 66-90). All reciprocal routes need a dated, flow-scoped qualification; November raw lines 9-18 contain only variant links.

Old iOS/Android dynamic-PaymentIntent examples set usd (old raw lines 1051-1069, 1300-1317) although the same branches' currency tables and Elements error table say Alma only supports eur (old raw lines 1194-1200, 1413-1419, 703-712). This old-source internal conflict warrants a reciprocal warning in the source and relevant concept; the example cannot establish USD support.

Old Android prose names PaymentHandler.confirmPayment, but the code uses PaymentLauncher.confirm (old raw lines 1362-1405), so code symbol selection needs variant/SDK verification rather than unqualified assertion.
unresolved_questions: November variant links were not pinned/read as full pages, so no November-specific flow, supported currency, SDK version, or outcome is verified (new raw lines 11-18).

The old mobile usd-versus-eur and Android confirm-class contradictions need separately pinned current authority before executable or eligibility guidance is given (old raw lines 1051-1069, 1194-1200, 1300-1317, 1362-1419).

findings: Add the November index as a separate navigation raw and date the May detailed claims (new raw lines 9-18; source lines 4-7, 29-31; old raw lines 1-10).
Correct four-path summary to include Android as an old-documented and new-listed route, without claiming a November feature addition (source line 13; old raw lines 1220-1226; new raw lines 16-18).

Scope return_url to Alma PaymentIntent confirmation, distinguish hosted versus embedded Checkout, and state browser return/QR closure versus PaymentIntent succeeded/capture boundaries (source lines 19-25; old raw lines 40-90, 488-497, 605-651, 703-712). Reciprocally qualify the same May claim at wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md lines 91 and 259 and wiki/stripe-index.md line 329 so a hosted Checkout query does not inherit a false universal requirement; new raw lines 9-18 establish no current requirement.
Warn that old mobile USD dynamic examples conflict with EUR-only tables/error and that Android prose/code name different confirmation APIs (old raw lines 1051-1069, 1194-1200, 1300-1317, 1362-1419).
conflicts: Source lines 13 and 19 conflict with old/new route and return_url evidence; wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md lines 91 and 259 and wiki/stripe-index.md line 329 repeat the unqualified return_url claim that conflicts with May hosted Checkout success_url versus PaymentIntent confirmation and embedded Checkout return_url (old raw lines 40-90, 392-394, 703-712). Old raw mobile examples conflict internally on currency and Android API naming at lines 1051-1069, 1194-1200, 1300-1317, 1362-1419.
source_assessments.reason: The November raw is navigation-only, but baseline summary omits a central Android route and overgeneralizes a PaymentIntent return_url requirement. The BNPL concept and Stripe index repeat the latter claim and require reciprocal qualification for hosted Checkout (concept lines 91, 259; index line 329; old raw lines 40-90, 703-712). The old raw itself has consequential mobile currency/example conflict needing a dated warning.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/alma/accept-a-payment, the complete November capture establishes only purpose and five variant links: Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS and Android (new raw lines 5-18). The May 6 detailed capture describes single-use Alma installments, server-created Checkout Sessions or PaymentIntents, same-currency Checkout line items, EUR support in its currency tables, customer redirect/authorization, status verification, and conditional manual capture (old raw lines 18-38, 127-168, 488-497, 621-651, 938-945). source-stripe-alma-accept-payment.md covers expiry, desktop QR, return URL, capture and errors but incorrectly calls this four paths and omits Android; its return_url statement must be scoped to PaymentIntent confirmation rather than hosted Checkout (source lines 13-27; old raw lines 40-90, 703-712, 1220-1226). The same unqualified historical claim recurs in wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md lines 91 and 259 and wiki/stripe-index.md line 329; these reciprocal routes also need a flow-scoped correction.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/alma/accept-a-payment, the new 18-line index is presentation/navigation, with no proven change to payment behavior or deprecation (new raw lines 9-18; diff lines 3-20, 1438-1443). source-stripe-alma-accept-payment.md should retain May 6 details as dated evidence: Elements mobile redirect versus desktop QR, one-hour requires_action expiry and at most 20 QR refreshes, conditional manual capture requiring later capture within seven days, and payment_intent.succeeded verification rather than browser-return success (old raw lines 605-673, 693-701). Its unqualified return_url line 19 must be scoped to PaymentIntent confirmation, and reciprocal wording at wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md lines 91 and 259 and wiki/stripe-index.md line 329 must distinguish hosted Checkout success_url from embedded Checkout return_url (old raw lines 40-90, 392-394, 703-712). The November index establishes no current return_url rule (new raw lines 9-18). The old iOS/Android USD dynamic examples contradict their EUR-only currency tables and error code, so the source and concept need a reciprocal warning, not inferred USD Alma eligibility (old raw lines 1051-1069, 1194-1200, 1300-1317, 1413-1419). Android old prose/code also differ on PaymentHandler versus PaymentLauncher (old raw lines 1362-1405). No live eligibility, account access, or payment completion follows from the index or samples.
